title: Fixture Landlord v Tenant (SCA) [TEST]
facts: A commercial landlord cancelled a lease for late payment without notice. The High Court set the cancellation aside. The landlord appeals.
grounds_of_appeal: The lease clause allowed cancellation on any late payment.
No notice was required on a proper reading of the clause.

grounds: The cancellation clause is clear and was triggered by late payment.
The High Court rewrote a commercial bargain.
Cancellation without notice is contrary to good faith in this lease.
The clause must be read with the notice provision in clause 14.

issues: Whether notice was required before cancellation.
Whether the clause is enforceable as written.
press_questions: Counsel, where in the lease is notice dispensed with in clear words?
reason_paragraphs: 1. The cancellation clause must be read with clause 14's notice requirement.
2. On these facts, cancellation without notice could not stand.
bench_notes.real_holding: Appeal dismissed. Notice was required before cancellation.

real_holding: Appeal dismissed. Notice was required before cancellation.
